requirement: Implement and verify all Epic 4 stories: make the complete 64-step score dominant, keep the pad as a secondary translator, make controls mode-aware and compact, and close the desktop accessibility/UAT gaps.

architecture.decision: Use one responsive CSS workspace with a full-width score plane as the visual anchor, a narrow translator rail for the pad and status, and compact action/control rails that reuse the existing React component seams. Keep all layout state derived from the existing pattern, mode, bank, transport, and guidance state.
alternatives: Keep the current equal two-pane chassis and tune only cell widths.
Add a separate desktop-only grid implementation beside the existing workspace.
tradeoffs: A single score plane gives all 64 columns a stable shared width at the 1280px floor, but requires moving the existing chassis regions into a new shell.
Reusing StepGrid, BeatPad, TransportControls, LayerStack, and utility dialogs avoids a parallel interaction model while allowing their visual hierarchy to change.
seams: src/App.tsx owns the workspace order and status copy.
src/theme.css and src/Device.css own the desktop shell and translator rail geometry.
src/StepGrid.css owns the score plane, bar/beat grouping, row rail, and playhead visibility.
src/TransportControls.tsx/.css and src/LayerStack.tsx/.css own the compact controls and lesson action strip.
src/Modal.tsx/.css and src/LessonLibrary.tsx/.css own keyboard-safe utility confirmation/error states.
